To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the floristic and phytosocial structure of a fragment of forest in the extreme south of the Atlantic Forest Biome were evaluated and the species with greater abundance were identified, which can be used as a tool for the restoration of degraded areas in this region.
the species Trichilia claissenii, Soroceabonplandii, Nectandra megopotamica, Actinostemom concolor and Apuleia leiocardapresented expressive abundance and distribution in different size classes.
the species with higher abundance and distribution in the different size class can be used as species for restoration of the forest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of species that can be used as a basis for restoration of areas in process, in the extreme South Atlantic Forest Biome.
the use of phytosociology for the identification of species for forest restoration in the extreme South Atlantic Forest Biome.
the importance of the use of phytosociology to the forest restoration, since it enables the identification of the most representative species of the area in the different size layers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the phytosociology in studies of the forest structure, besides allowing the identification of species that are important to the maintenance of the ecosystem, also provides information on the species that can be used for the restoration of degraded areas.
the species that presented a greater representativeness in all the layers were Trichilia clausseni, Sorocea boplândii, Actinostenon concolor, Apulia leiocarpa and Machaerum paraguariense.

the study of the forest structure in the different size layers, through the use of the phytosociology, allows the evaluation of the species with the greatest potential for the recovery of the degraded area, thus enabling the restoration of the forest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the species of the pioneer and intermediate layers can be used in enrichment of areas with low cover of vegetation in the scope of forest restoration, whereas the species of the arboreal layer can be used in areas that are in the process of regeneration.

, although it is not possible to establish a relationship between the species of each size class, the most abundant species can be used as a guide in the moment of enrichment of the area in process of restoration.

it is possible to use the knowledge of phytosociology in the process of restoration of degraded areas, since it allows the identification of species with potential for enrichment and/or planting in the area.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the species with greater representativeness in a given layer can be used in enrichment, as well as the species with greater abundance can be used in planting, since they are the species most adapted to the local conditions.
it is possible to identify the potential species of restoration of the area studied, through a simple and fast method, which can be replicated in other areas of the biome.

the species of pioneer and initial secondary are the ones that are most represented in the different layers, and they should be considered as the main candidates to the enrichment of areas that are in the process of restoration.
